exposure: maternal serum concentrations of vitamin D early in pregnancy
cohort: The study included 269 women whose children were born preterm (< 37 gestational weeks) (cases) and 332 women whose children were born term (>= 37 gestational weeks) (controls), all of whom gave birth in Scania, Sweden.
finding: Although all comparisons showed adjusted odds ratios indicating that low maternal vitamin D concentrations early in pregnancy might increase the risk of preterm birth, none of these associations reached statistical significance, providing no to very weak support for an association.
gest_age: Preterm (< 37 gestational weeks), term (>= 37 gestational weeks); subgroups: extreme preterm (< 28 gw), severe preterm (28-32 gw), and late preterm (33-36 gw).
